title: Rate and speed: d = s × t
subject: math

doNow.prompt: A bus travels at 60 km/h. How far has it really travelled after half an hour?

choices.misconception: 60 km/h means the bus has travelled 60 km.

rationale.chose: The learner selected option 60 km as their answer to this question.
rationale.thinks: They are applying the coded wrong turn instead of reading the speed as a distance per hour.
rationale.reteach: Reteach from the paired notes trap: 60 km/h means the bus has travelled 60 km.. A rate is read as a total instead of an amount per unit of time. Speed is distance per hour: after half an hour at 60 km/h the bus has gone 30 km, not 60. In the animation scene s3 the claim is tested against the road and fails: after half an hour the bus sits at the 30 km mark, not the 60 km mark.
